data.body:
Module-size note (surfaced by this change, tracked separately): annotating the 12 `repo_root` params pushed four signatures past the line-length limit, so `ruff format` wrapped them. authorship.py went 784 -> 793 LOC against the hard 800 cap. This change PASSES the module-size gate, but leaves only 7 lines of headroom, so the next routine edit to the file would trip the CI gate on an unrelated author. Re-wrapping is not an option (the layout is `ruff format` output and `make lint` runs `ruff format --check`), so the fix is a split. Filed as courageous-deserving-manatee (760f-608f-4c69-449a), linked discovered_from this ticket, proposing a split along the already-existing git-ancestry/commit-resolution seam (the five resolve_*/build_*_map functions, ~330 LOC) with public import paths re-exported — several tests reach these as `authorship.<name>` attributes and at least one monkeypatches through that path.

No latent bugs were revealed by the annotations: every call site already passed `str` for repo_root (tests pass `str(store)` / `str(tmp_path)`), and both `keys_valid_at_anchor` callers and the single `position_resolver` caller match the annotated callable shapes exactly.
